column1: # tools/stale-areas.tsv - the areas of this repository, and when each was last audited.
# READ BY tools/check_stale_area.py. That tool's docstring says why this file
# exists, what a row means, and why the answer is "areas and dates", never
# "documents and sentences".
# WHERE THESE AREAS COME FROM. Queue item 10 (docs/HANDOFF-AFTER-PR39.md:300)
# says "list areas changed since their last audit; the coverage map from this
# session is the template". The template is
# docs/audit-reports-2026-09-29-30/37-audit-a84616c6.md, a meta-audit asked
# "What are we missing? Which areas have not been audited for a long time, or
# ever?". THE AREAS BELOW ARE THAT REPORT'S AREAS, in its order. Its own Key is
# the verdict column's vocabulary:
#     NEVER = no report names it. STALE = audited, but the code changed since.
# ITS GLOBS ARE THIS FILE'S TRANSCRIPTION, and they are meant to be edited: the
# coverage map's areas are prose ("Phone screens (about 60 Plates)", "Backend
# chatbot driver and support (about 15 modules)") and a checker cannot read
# prose. Where a row below says "never", no report has ever named that area -
# the report's own words, not this file's opinion.
# HOW TO KEEP IT HONEST. A row goes quiet when its area has not changed since
# `last_audited`. When an audit happens, move that date forward and put the
# report that did it in `evidence`. Moving a date WITHOUT an audit is the one
# thing this file must never carry: it is the difference between a record and a
# way to make a checker green. `last_audited` is the date of the newest report
# that AUDITED the area - a report that examined it and said what it found. A
# page that merely names a file (docs/JARVIS-API.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) is
# not an audit and must never set a date here; that was checked, and using such
# a mention would have cleared nearly every row below on no evidence at all.
# TWO ROWS WERE CORRECTED ON 2026-10-16, AND THE REASON IS THE POINT:
#   * `phone-screen-watch-avatar` said "never". The coverage map wrote that on
#     2026-09-30, and both files were audited afterwards -
#     docs/BUG-AUDIT-2026-10-05.md names both, and
#     docs/audit-2026-10-07/C-android-kotlin.md names ScreenWatchService.kt
#     again at three separate findings. Both files' newest change is
#     2026-09-30 (ceaf1db6), so the row is now QUIET, and it is the one row here
#     that proves the tool can go green. The map was stale, not the code.
#   * `videos` was listed "NEVER (fine)" and is NOT a row at all: 222 files, a
#     change on 2026-10-07 (505118ad, "the launch videos move to a release"),
#     and nothing in a video to audit. A row for it would be a false positive
#     every time it was read, which is how a checker teaches people to ignore it.
#     The report's "NEVER (fine)" is kept here, which is where a dismissal
#     belongs.
# COLUMNS, tab-separated, five of them, one row per area:
#     area          a short name, unique in this file
#     globs         comma-separated git pathspecs; a directory covers its tree
#     last_audited  YYYY-MM-DD, or "never" when no report names the area
#     verdict       the coverage map's own word for the area as it recorded it
#     evidence      the report that did the audit, or "-" when there is none
# A row whose globs match no tracked file is reported as a broken row, never as
# a pass. Adding an area is one line; removing one is a decision, so say why.
